title: Docks and Yard Access
before:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

2. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Position inbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-01 Inbound receiving for arrival, document check and unloading.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

6. For inbound operations, report to the inbound waiting area at your booked time slot. Present documents at Zone A for the document check in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Wait for the dispatcher to call you forward to doors 1-4.

7. For outbound operations, stage loads in Zone D in front of docks 5-8. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Do not load past the assigned door and do not release a load without dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

9. Observe yard and dock speed limits at all times:

10. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

title: Vehicle Loads and Outbound Capacity
before:
1. Execute all outbound movements under PR-06 Outbound dispatch from Zone D.

All loading, door moves and vehicle releases for PR-06 Outbound dispatch are performed from Zone D. Do not stage or release outbound loads from any other zone.

2. Use only docks 5-8 for outbound dispatch. The site provides 4 outbound dock doors for this purpose.

Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and confirms door numbers before any pallet is moved to the dock.

3. Obtain the dispatcher's confirmed door assignment before transferring any pallet to the dock. Do not move loads to docks 5-8 without that confirmation.

Hold pallets in Zone D staging until the dispatcher has communicated the assigned door to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carrier. Move to the dock only after that confirmation is recorded.

4. Verify PR-05 Packing and labelling is completed in full before release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Stage only stretch-wrapped pallets in Zone D.

PR-05 Packing and labelling must be completed in full before any load is released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Every outbound pallet must be stretch-wrapped prior to placement in outbound staging. Do not stage unwrapped pallets.

5. Observe the pallet limit: a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Check gross weight on the scanner record before assigning vehicle type.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Weigh-check any pallet suspected to be overweight. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

6. Load contracted curtain-side trailers within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 26000 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 33 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, payload governs capacity. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

Do not exceed either the payload limit or the floor positions. For full-weight pallets, plan to a maximum of 28 pallets per trailer.

7. Load the delivery van within both limits:
   a. Payload limit is 1800 kg.
   b. Floor capacity is 6 pallet positions.
   c. At maximum pallet weight, the van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets. Route any heavier order by trailer.

Check both weight and floor positions before assigning the van. If the order exceeds 2 full-weight pallets, book trailer capacity and do not split a full-weight pallet across vehicles.

8. Plan door utilisation per shift. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.

Coordinate with the dispatcher to sequence bookings across the 4 outbound doors. Keep each door to its planned 3 loads per shift and avoid queuing trailers outside the assigned time slots.

9. Calculate outbound capacity on full-weight pallets. With 4 doors each handling 3 loads of 28 pallets, outbound capacity is at most 336 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer). Schedule bookings within that ceiling and refer overflow to the next shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 336 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.

Do not exceed the calculated ceiling without prior agreement. Record all bookings in the WMS and refer excess demand to the next available shift.

10. Respect hazmat constraints when staging mixed loads. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage inside Zone F at one time. At maximum pallet weight this equates to at most 4 full-weight pallets (hazmat stock limit divided by maximum pallet weight). Do not allocate hazmat pallets to a trailer until cage stock is confirmed within limit.

Stage hazmat only inside the hazmat cage in Zone F. Confirm the cage total is within limit before building any outbound hazmat load.

11. Record trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts in the WMS before releasing the vehicle. Report any overweight pallet or over-limit staging to the shift supervisor immediately.

Trailer and van loads, door numbers and pallet counts must be recorded in the WMS before the vehicle is released. Do not release until the dispatcher has verified the record and loading and door checks are complete.

title: 1.3 Dispatcher - Transport Booking and Dock Scheduling
before:
1. The dispatcher is accountable for outbound flow from Zone D. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.

2. Duties of the dispatcher are:
   1. Book transport for all outbound orders.
   2. Assign dock doors and time slots to carriers.
   3. Release outbound loads under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only when loads are complete and documented.

3. Operate the building's 8 dock doors as a single coordinated plan:
   1. Reserve dock doors 1-4 for inbound receiving.
   2. Reserve dock doors 5-8 for outbound dispatch.
   3. There are 4 outbound dock doors available for scheduling.

4. Own the dock schedule:
   1. Assign each carrier a specific door number and time slot.
   2. Balance demand across doors to maintain throughput.
   3. Communicate door assignments to the shift supervisor, forklift operators and carriers before loading.

5. Enforce staging discipline in Zone D:
   1. Stage only verified and packed pallets in outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
   2. Do not release loads where picked items have not been scan-verified before packing in accordance with PR-04 and PR-05.

6. Apply load limits on every booking:
   1. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg.
   2. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 26000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions.
   3. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
   4. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1800 kg and has 6 pallet positions.
   5. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

7. Plan shift capacity to the proven maximum:
   1. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
   2. With 4 outbound dock doors, each taking at most 28 full-weight pallets per trailer, outbound capacity is at most 336 full-weight pallets per shift.
   3. Do not overbook beyond this limit. Split excess volume to the next shift or add trailer capacity beyond the 336 full-weight pallet per shift limit with warehouse manager agreement.

8. Execute PR-06 Outbound dispatch as follows:
   1. Confirm order completeness and packing completion before assigning a door.
   2. Assign door and time slot and record them in the system.
   3. Release the load only after loading and door checks are complete.

9. Coordinate handover at shift change:
   1. Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover with the outgoing and incoming shift supervisors.
   2. Hand over open bookings, door allocations, delayed trailers and van commitments.
   3. Ensure no carrier arrives without a confirmed door and time slot.

title: 1.2 Dispatch Times and Load Release
before:
Harborwick 3PL Ltd. commits to dispatch operations from Zone D, the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. The building has 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors.

1. Order preparation starts in Zone C, the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, where pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2. Pick faces are replenished under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces before the picking shift starts. PR-04 Order picking is then executed on replenished faces.
3. Picked items are scan-verified before packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling. No order proceeds to PR-05 Packing and labelling without scan verification.
4. Packing, labelling and wrapping for PR-05 Packing and labelling and PR-06 Outbound dispatch are completed in Zone D. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers in Zone D for outbound pallets.
5. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers for docks 5-8 and confirms door assignment before loading.

Shift capacity is measured per operating shift. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

6. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. With 4 outbound doors, total outbound throughput is scheduled on this basis.
7. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 26000 kg and have 33 floor pallet positions. A trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, calculated as payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
8. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1800 kg and has 6 pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
9. Outbound capacity is at most 336 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as doors multiplied by loads per shift multiplied by pallets per trailer. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 336 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.
10. Loads are released under PR-06 Outbound dispatch only after packing and verification under PR-05 Packing and labelling are complete, pallets are wrapped, and door checks are satisfied. The dispatcher is the sole role to release the vehicle for departure.

title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 26000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1800 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 336 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 3 loads per shift multiplied by 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 336 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.
